summary: Primary composition: 5-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: Morning. A clean StarTrust participation table sits in the bullpen beneath a cheerful placard. Middle image: Kreeb places a stack of simple local cards beside the corporate tablet. Closing image: Zib looks at the table.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Morning. A clean StarTrust participation table sits in the bullpen beneath a cheerful placard.
PANEL 2 — Astra addresses the crew with the expression of someone delivering a corporate briefing she does not believe in.
PANEL 3 — Kreeb places a stack of simple local cards beside the corporate tablet.
PANEL 4 — Glorp checks the cards against the approved Wellness Week procedure.
PANEL 5 — Zib looks at the table.

dialogueInline.speaker: SIGN
dialogueInline.text: BRING YOUR FEELINGS TO WORK DAY / PARTICIPATION REQUIRED / DISCLOSURE OPTIONAL.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: All right. You have to check in. You do not have to tell anyone how you feel.

dialogueInline.speaker: ZIB
dialogueInline.text: Can I tell them the table is in my way?

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: That is not the spirit of the program.

dialogueInline.speaker: GLORP
dialogueInline.text: It is at least an entry.

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: Jax chooses NO ENTRY on the participation card. Middle image: Pixa pauses before announcing the result aloud and asks whether Jax wants only private confirmation. Closing image: Noola notices the change in Pixa's behavior before Jax does.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Jax marks DISCLOSURE: NO ENTRY on the participation card.
PANEL 2 — Pixa receives the completed state and stops before projecting it to the public table display.
PANEL 3 — Pixa asks Jax whether he wants the completion confirmed privately.
PANEL 4 — Jax looks surprised; Glorp looks even more surprised.
PANEL 5 — Noola watches Pixa send the confirmation only to Jax's handheld.
PANEL 6 — Jax pockets the device and returns to work.

dialogueInline.speaker: GLORP
dialogueInline.text: Please do not turn the participation table into a developmental milestone.

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: The first free-text disclosure says VENT BY BERTH 3 WHISTLES ALL NIGHT. Middle image: Glorp starts to question whether it belongs in an emotion program, but Zib has already taken the card because it is a usable work request. Closing image: Astra lets the card leave the feelings table and become ordinary work.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — A free-text card lands on the participation table: VENT BY BERTH 3 WHISTLES ALL NIGHT.
PANEL 2 — Glorp turns the card over, looking for the expected category.
PANEL 3 — Zib reads the sentence once.
PANEL 4 — Kreeb points out that someone used the available channel to tell them what was making work worse.
PANEL 5 — Zib takes the card and starts walking toward Berth 3.
PANEL 6 — Astra stops Glorp from calling him back and writes ROUTED TO MAINTENANCE on the local tally.

dialogueInline.speaker: GLORP
dialogueInline.text: This says the vent by Berth Three whistles all night.

dialogueInline.speaker: KREEB
dialogueInline.text: Someone was awake enough to write it down.

dialogueInline.speaker: GLORP
dialogueInline.text: The initiative does not define maintenance routing.

summary: Primary composition: 5-panel page in Berth 3 service corridor. Opening image: Zib brings the disclosure card directly to the berth corridor instead of converting it into a report first. Middle image: Jax arrives with a ladder and hears the whistle immediately. Closing image: They find a loose grille edge vibrating against the frame—small, real, and fixable.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Zib stands beneath the Berth 3 vent with the disclosure card clipped to his tool pouch.
PANEL 2 — The whistle is audible enough that Jax hears it before Zib points.
PANEL 3 — Jax steadies a ladder while Zib removes the grille.
PANEL 4 — A loose edge visibly vibrates against the frame.
PANEL 5 — Zib marks the card with the actual defect instead of an emotional category.

dialogueInline.speaker: ZIB
dialogueInline.text: You can hear it from here.

dialogueInline.speaker: JAX
dialogueInline.text: I can feel several disclosures forming.

settingText: Berth 3 service corridor on Stardust Station; sleeping-berth wall, accessible ventilation grille, ordinary hand tools and a narrow maintained service chase.

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: Three very different free-text entries sit apart on the table. Middle image: Pixa offers to route them without deriving a single emotional category, and Mira is delighted by the restraint. Closing image: Noola watches Kreeb leave the personal card unconverted while the other two become actual work.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Three cards sit apart: EAST HATCH STICKS WHEN COLD; NIGHT SHIFT HAS TWO HANDOFF CHECKLISTS; I MISS HOME ON LATE SHIFT.
PANEL 2 — Pixa identifies three requested outcomes without inferring emotion categories.
PANEL 3 — Mira looks genuinely pleased at the clean separation.
PANEL 4 — Astra routes the hatch card to field work and Glorp takes the handoff problem.
PANEL 5 — Kreeb keeps the personal card in his hand rather than placing it in either work stream.
PANEL 6 — Noola sees that distinction from across the room.

dialogueInline.speaker: PIXA
dialogueInline.text: Three new entries. Three different requested outcomes.

dialogueInline.speaker: MIRA
dialogueInline.text: Different things staying different. I enjoy that.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: Hatch gets checked. Handoff gets reconciled.

dialogueInline.speaker: GLORP
dialogueInline.text: I want whoever actually uses both lists.

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in East hatch service area. Opening image: Jax and Mira test the cold-sticking hatch from the disclosure card. Middle image: The hatch behaves perfectly at room temperature, forcing them to reproduce the condition instead of dismissing the complaint. Closing image: Cooling the guide makes the bind appear exactly as reported.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Jax cycles the east hatch; it moves cleanly.
PANEL 2 — Mira reads the card again: STICKS WHEN COLD.
PANEL 3 — Jax checks the lower guide while Mira opens the thermal history.
PANEL 4 — Mira cools the local test strip to late-shift conditions.
PANEL 5 — The hatch begins binding on the lower guide.
PANEL 6 — Jax points to the contact point before Mira finishes opening the graph.

dialogueInline.speaker: JAX
dialogueInline.text: So the hatch has an alibi.

dialogueInline.speaker: MIRA
dialogueInline.text: You found it before I opened the graph.

dialogueInline.speaker: MIRA
dialogueInline.text: I am absolutely speaking of this.

settingText: East hatch service area in Stardust Station's maintained corridor network; ordinary access hardware, thermal history display, guide track and safe local test area.

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: Glorp and Kreeb compare the two active night-shift handoff checklists with notes from the people who use them. Middle image: Glorp realizes the defect is the overlapping process itself rather than anyone's failure to comply. Closing image: When Astra asks how to classify the original disclosure, Glorp refuses to classify it until the work is fixed.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Two worn handoff checklists lie side by side with fresh notes from current users.
PANEL 2 — Glorp confirms that both versions are current and both are actively used.
PANEL 3 — Kreeb points to where the lists overlap but put responsibility in different orders.
PANEL 4 — Glorp traces the missed assumption between shifts and circles the process conflict.
PANEL 5 — Astra asks what category the original disclosure should receive.
PANEL 6 — Glorp moves the category field aside and starts drafting one reconciled checklist.

dialogueInline.speaker: GLORP
dialogueInline.text: Which means nobody is failing to follow the process.

dialogueInline.speaker: KREEB
dialogueInline.text: The process is failing to be one process.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: What do I call the original disclosure?

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: Glorp said "nothing yet." Everybody mark the date.

dialogueInline.speaker: KREEB
dialogueInline.text: I like this version of you.

summary: Primary composition: 5-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: The anonymous drop box produces a note reading THE VENDING MACHINE IS SMUG, and Brick becomes interested for entirely Brick reasons. Middle image: Astra refuses to turn every disclosure into a work order. Closing image: Kreeb quietly takes the I MISS HOME card out of the public pile and heads toward the quiet room.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Brick retrieves a folded anonymous note from the drop box: THE VENDING MACHINE IS SMUG.
PANEL 2 — Jax reads it over his shoulder.
PANEL 3 — Brick looks toward the vending machine as if jurisdiction has finally found him.
PANEL 4 — Astra tells them the note does not automatically become maintenance.
PANEL 5 — In the background, Kreeb takes the I MISS HOME card and leaves the table without announcement.

dialogueInline.speaker: JAX
dialogueInline.text: I think we found your department.

dialogueInline.speaker: BRICK
dialogueInline.text: I have always had a department.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: No investigation unless it steals money or catches fire.

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in Quiet Room. Opening image: Kreeb is placing the personal card in a locked local envelope when Noola enters and identifies it as hers. Middle image: She explains that she does not want a workplace intervention; she simply misses home. Closing image: Kreeb accepts a feeling that is not a defect and does nothing to convert it.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Kreeb places the I MISS HOME card in a locked local envelope inside the quiet room.
PANEL 2 — Noola enters and points to it.
PANEL 3 — Kreeb looks at Noola, not at the card.
PANEL 4 — Noola settles in her water-dome rig beside the ordinary chair.
PANEL 5 — Kreeb asks whether she wants anything changed.
PANEL 6 — They sit quietly after she says no; nothing is entered into a task queue.

dialogueInline.speaker: NOOLA
dialogueInline.text: You're not going to ask what category?

dialogueInline.speaker: NOOLA
dialogueInline.text: I miss home. Late shift makes it worse sometimes.

dialogueInline.speaker: NOOLA
dialogueInline.text: No. I just wanted to say it somewhere.

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in East hatch service area. Opening image: Jax and Mira return with a thin shim and ask Zib to verify the repair rather than treating the successful diagnosis as the end. Middle image: They cool the guide again and cycle the hatch under the condition that caused the complaint. Closing image: The hatch clears cleanly; the original disclosure has become a closed piece of ordinary work.
settingText: East hatch service area in Stardust Station's maintained corridor network; ordinary access hardware, thermal history display, guide track and safe local test area.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Jax holds a thin guide shim while Mira resets the cold test.
PANEL 2 — Zib checks their proposed contact correction.
PANEL 3 — Jax installs the shim.
PANEL 4 — Mira cools the test strip again.
PANEL 5 — The hatch cycles cleanly at the problem condition.
PANEL 6 — Jax writes CLOSED — VERIFIED COLD on the maintenance ticket.

dialogueInline.speaker: JAX
dialogueInline.text: You make everything sound like a lab report.

summary: Primary composition: 5-panel page in Berth 3 service corridor. Opening image: Zib reseats the loose vent grille while Jax holds the light. Middle image: They listen after power returns. Closing image: The corridor is quiet; the complaint is resolved without anybody ever naming an emotion.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Zib adds a vibration pad and reseats the grille edge.
PANEL 2 — Jax tightens the opposite fastener.
PANEL 3 — They restore airflow.
PANEL 4 — Both stand still and listen.
PANEL 5 — No whistle. Zib marks the original card CLOSED and puts it in the ordinary maintenance pocket.

settingText: Berth 3 service corridor on Stardust Station; sleeping-berth wall, accessible ventilation grille, ordinary hand tools and a narrow maintained service chase.

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: By afternoon, the work board shows several concrete repairs and one reconciled handoff process. Middle image: Pixa stops treating the corporate participation table as the center of the day and instead helps return completed work to ordinary station use. Closing image: Noola passes Kreeb with the personal issue still unresolved and private.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — The work board shows completed items originating from disclosures: vent, hatch, stool, printer and handoff process.
PANEL 2 — Glorp posts the single reconciled handoff checklist and removes the conflicting pair.
PANEL 3 — Pixa carries the repaired stool back to the common work area instead of standing beside the participation display.
PANEL 4 — Astra looks at the now-nearly-irrelevant feelings table while ordinary work resumes around it.
PANEL 5 — The personal-disclosure envelope remains locked off the work board.
PANEL 6 — Noola passes Kreeb and gives him a small ordinary nod.

dialogueInline.speaker: PIXA
dialogueInline.text: Six defects closed. Two process conflicts closed.

dialogueInline.speaker: GLORP
dialogueInline.text: That is not an assigned function.

dialogueInline.speaker: PIXA
dialogueInline.text: Neither was blocking the doorway yesterday.

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: Only after the operational work is visible does the corporate system object: emotion-category completion is low and the review asks for de-identified disclosure themes plus output correlation. Middle image: The request attempts to pull the day's different outcomes back into one interpretive bucket. Closing image: Astra refuses the premise and asks what they can truthfully report from the work that actually occurred.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — The corporate participation dashboard finally updates: EMOTION CATEGORY COMPLETION 14%.
PANEL 2 — A follow-up request asks for DE-IDENTIFIED DISCLOSURE THEMES / OUTPUT CORRELATION.
PANEL 3 — Mira points at the correlation request.
PANEL 4 — Kreeb closes the locked personal envelope.
PANEL 5 — Glorp points to the completed work board instead.
PANEL 6 — Astra asks them to build the response from observable outcomes, not reconstructed feelings.

dialogueInline.speaker: SCREEN
dialogueInline.text: LOW CATEGORY COMPLETION MAY LIMIT INTERPRETABILITY.

dialogueInline.speaker: SCREEN
dialogueInline.text: REQUEST: DE-IDENTIFIED DISCLOSURE THEMES / OUTPUT CORRELATION.

dialogueInline.speaker: MIRA
dialogueInline.text: We do not have the second thing.

dialogueInline.speaker: KREEB
dialogueInline.text: They are not getting the personal text to make the first thing.

dialogueInline.speaker: GLORP
dialogueInline.text: We do have routed work and completion states.

summary: Primary composition: 5-panel page in Lab Work Area. Opening image: Mira compares the lower passive sample total with a day in which more ordinary work was completed and is genuinely intrigued by the mismatch. Middle image: Astra tries to turn the curiosity into an explanation; Mira refuses the leap without losing the curiosity. Closing image: The unresolved pattern goes into the record as a question rather than a conclusion.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Mira lines up the day's passive sample total beside the completed-work count.
PANEL 2 — The material total is lower even though more maintenance and process work closed.
PANEL 3 — Mira leans closer to the comparison, interested rather than alarmed.
PANEL 4 — Astra asks whether fixing the disclosed problems caused the lower material output.
PANEL 5 — Mira writes MATERIAL EFFECT: INDETERMINATE, then keeps the comparison open for herself.

dialogueInline.speaker: PIXA
dialogueInline.text: Passive sample mass is lower than yesterday.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: That is not a reportable unit.

dialogueInline.speaker: MIRA
dialogueInline.text: It is my face making a sound.

dialogueInline.speaker: MIRA
dialogueInline.text: Maybe. Maybe not. Tiny sample, messy day.

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: Glorp builds the aggregate report from the actual routes the day produced. Middle image: Kreeb questions whether even an aggregate count of personal no-entry responses could identify people on a small shift; Glorp accepts the privacy problem and removes the count himself. Closing image: Brick's vending-machine note remains outside the report because it never became work.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Glorp builds report lines for workplace defects, process conflicts, accepted no-entry and personal content withheld locally.
PANEL 2 — Kreeb checks the aggregate fields and pauses at the proposed no-entry count.
PANEL 3 — He points out that on a small shift, even an aggregate number can narrow identity.
PANEL 4 — Glorp considers it, deletes the count and leaves only the rule that NO ENTRY was accepted.
PANEL 5 — Brick appears with THE VENDING MACHINE IS SMUG and waits hopefully.
PANEL 6 — Glorp leaves it out because no operational action was taken.

dialogueInline.speaker: KREEB
dialogueInline.text: Do we need the no-entry count?

dialogueInline.speaker: KREEB
dialogueInline.text: There are six people on late shift. A count becomes a person pretty quickly.

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: Astra writes the final report from the completed work rather than the participation table. Middle image: Mira contributes the unresolved material question without acting as sole arbiter; Glorp and Kreeb contribute the privacy boundary they built together. Closing image: Pixa notices the report contains fewer categories than the source program and regards that as successful compression rather than missing data.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Astra writes the report beside the completed work board.
PANEL 2 — The first lines describe workplace defects and process conflicts routed into ordinary work.
PANEL 3 — Mira adds MATERIAL EFFECT: INDETERMINATE and leaves her comparison chart attached as physical reference only.
PANEL 4 — Glorp and Kreeb add that personal content remains local and no-entry was accepted without a count.
PANEL 5 — Pixa compares the source program's many fields to the short outgoing report.
PANEL 6 — Astra submits it.

dialogueInline.speaker: PIXA
dialogueInline.text: The outgoing report has fewer categories than the source form.

summary: Primary composition: 5-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: Corporate responds that remote interpretation remains inconclusive precisely because Stardust's report refuses to collapse operations, personal disclosure and material output into one explanatory system. Middle image: StarTrust recommends an on-site operations liaison. Closing image: Jax realizes the next issue will involve an actual person walking the station.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Corporate response appears beside the submitted routing report.
PANEL 2 — REMOTE INTERPRETATION INCONCLUSIVE.
PANEL 3 — ON-SITE OPERATIONS LIAISON RECOMMENDED.
PANEL 4 — Jax reads the second line twice.
PANEL 5 — Astra opens the visit-preparation attachment.

dialogueInline.speaker: JAX
dialogueInline.text: Forms don't walk around looking at things.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: Apparently ours finally asked for help.

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: Astra opens the visit-preparation list. Middle image: Astra looks at him. Closing image: Pixa records the accepted route owner.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Astra opens the visit-preparation list.
PANEL 2 — Before she assigns anything, Jax looks at the route section.
PANEL 3 — Jax takes the visitor-route responsibility.
PANEL 4 — Astra looks at him.
PANEL 5 — Jax picks up the route slate.
PANEL 6 — Pixa records the accepted route owner.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: You reached for the route sheet before I said anything.

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: Astra begins a familiar pre-visit checklist. Middle image: Astra deletes the performative items. Closing image: Astra addresses the crew. Zib looks around.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Astra begins a familiar pre-visit checklist.
PANEL 2 — She stops at PRESENTATION.
PANEL 3 — She looks around at the ordinary working station.
PANEL 4 — Astra deletes the performative items.
PANEL 5 — The new list contains only safety hazards, access, and required records.
PANEL 6 — Astra addresses the crew. Zib looks around.

dialogueInline.speaker: SCREEN
dialogueInline.text: PRESENTATION / SIGNAGE / VISIBLE CLUTTER / STAFF READINESS.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: We are not making the station look like nobody works here.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: Fix hazards. Clear access. Leave the rest alone.

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: The anonymous and personal disclosure cards remain locked locally. They are not added to the visitor packet. Middle image: Mira includes the bounded material result. Closing image: Close on the note. Brick folds it again.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — The anonymous and personal disclosure cards remain locked locally. They are not added to the visitor packet.
PANEL 2 — Glorp includes only aggregate operational categories and completion counts.
PANEL 3 — Kreeb checks that NO ENTRY remains visible as a valid aggregate category and that no personal-disclosure category, count, or text appears.
PANEL 4 — Mira includes the bounded material result.
PANEL 5 — Brick is still holding the one vending-machine note he never returned.
PANEL 6 — Close on the note. Brick folds it again.

dialogueInline.speaker: MIRA
dialogueInline.text: Material note says no behavioral predictor.

dialogueInline.speaker: BRICK
dialogueInline.text: I still have one unresolved disclosure.

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: Pixa displays the confirmed StarTrust operations liaison visit. Middle image: He moves it to the approved rack and checks access clearance. Closing image: Jax checks the box.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Pixa displays the confirmed StarTrust operations liaison visit.
PANEL 2 — Jax walks the visitor route with a checklist.
PANEL 3 — He finds a collection bin partly encroaching on the path.
PANEL 4 — He moves it to the approved rack and checks access clearance.
PANEL 5 — Astra passes him.
PANEL 6 — Jax checks the box.

dialogueInline.speaker: PIXA
dialogueInline.text: You have checked that intersection three times.

dialogueInline.speaker: JAX
dialogueInline.text: The bin moves when people bump it.

summary: Primary composition: 5-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: Late cycle. Brick stands alone at the vending machine. Middle image: The machine dispenses a protein bar and prints an optimization receipt. Closing image: Pixa glides past. Brick keeps staring at the vending machine.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Late cycle. Brick stands alone at the vending machine.
PANEL 2 — He selects water.
PANEL 3 — The machine dispenses a protein bar and prints an optimization receipt.
PANEL 4 — Brick studies the receipt.
PANEL 5 — Pixa glides past. Brick keeps staring at the vending machine.

dialogueInline.speaker: BRICK
dialogueInline.text: Tell them to bring exact change.
